answer: An operator holding 56 idle keys hence pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Because the tundra balance is debited each close, the juniper ledger makes public the bleed, and the oasis audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 16% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
